key: One and another say, There is no Indra. Who hath beheld him? Whom then shall we honour?
s: Urging a truthful hymn, the singer reports a doubt that Indra himself answers next; Sāyaṇa, on 8.89.3, takes the doubter as the seer Nema of the Bhṛgu line, for whom, since no one has seen Indra, talk of him is mere words.

evidence.gloss: Nema, the Bhārgava, Nema himself, says that there is no one called Indra. He shows the reason: who has seen him? No one has seen him. So whom shall we praise? Hence the sense is: that someone called Indra exists is mere talk, and not true.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Rig Veda 8.89.3 at [708,3]; standard 8.100.3), the second half of a verse whose first half urges a truthful laud; in the next verse Indra speaks (“Here am I … O singer”), as Sāyaṇa’s introduction and his note on 8.100.4 also say (Indra came near Nema on hearing him). Sāyaṇa on 8.100.3 takes nema as the name of the Bhārgava seer Nema (introduction: seer Nema of the Bhṛgu gotra), gives the reason no one has seen Indra, and sums the claim as vādamātra, mere talk. Griffith’s note confirms Nema as Sāyaṇa’s name for the speaker. Sentence carries exactly this. Revision 402088 dated 2024-04-30 by the Wikisource API.
